# Downtime dispatch stalls ~60 of every 62 minutes despite 3 free LLM slots — empty coordination file triggers the 1-hour no-candidate cooldown

## Problem statement

The downtime worker in coordination mode (`dispatchFromCoordination` + `tick` in `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts`) dispatches at most ~1 item per ~62 minutes **regardless of how many llama-proxy slots are free**. All 3 slots sit idle for ~60 of every 62 minutes with no polls, no file activity, and no dispatch. Observed on the Tableau-Card-Engine worklog (`CG`): dispatches at 19:28:03Z, 20:30:19Z, 21:32:44Z, 22:35:28Z — a stable 62–63 minute cadence confirmed live.

## Root cause chain (verified live with probes + file watches)

1. The coordination check-in (30-min cadence) offers exactly ONE entry — the instance's single most-important item (`runCoordinationCheckIn` → `computeMostImportantItem` → `upsertEntry`).
2. After a successful dispatch the leader REMOVES the entry → `downtime-coordination.json` is `entries: []`.
3. ~60 s later (the next idle period after the dispatch), the leader evaluates idle → dispatch attempt → `dispatchFromCoordination([], ...)` returns `{dispatched: false, reason: 'no-candidate'}`.
4. `tick()` treats this as a "genuine empty backlog" and enters `cooldownUntil = now + downtimeNoCandidateCooldownMs` (default **60 minutes**).
5. **The cooldown short-circuit sits BEFORE the check-in in `tick()`**, so the 30-min check-in (the only re-offer mechanism) is blocked for the whole pause.
6. On cooldown expiry the check-in runs once → offers the next item → 60 s idle threshold → dispatch → entry removed → 60 s later → empty file → `no-candidate` → cooldown → LOOP.

The `no-candidate` pause was designed for a *genuinely empty backlog* (docs, line ~59 of `downtime-worker.ts`) but is triggered by a *transiently empty coordination file* even when the worklog has plenty of dispatchable candidates (verified: `computeMostImportantItem` finds CG-0MTC31LN3000UHDY → implement at the same moment the file was empty and the worker was paused).

## Evidence

- `downtime-dispatches.log` (TCE): 19:28:03Z → 20:30:19Z → 21:32:44Z → 22:35:28Z (62/63-min gaps).
- File watch: `downtime-coordination.json` mtime frozen for the full cooldown, then written at cooldown expiry + 1 min (check-in), then dispatch ~60 s later (live: entry written 22:34:13Z, dispatch 22:35:28Z).
- Probe: `dispatchFromCoordination([], opts)` returns `{dispatched:false, reason:'no-candidate'}`; `evaluateIdle` returns `true` (3/3 slots free) throughout.
- Same cycle reproduced on ContextHub after downtime was enabled 22:46Z (check-in 22:46:31Z → dispatch 22:47:36Z → files frozen since).

## Required fix (ACs)

- [ ] AC1: A dispatch attempt against an empty coordination file must NOT enter the no-candidate cooldown while `computeMostImportantItem` (or an equivalent candidate query) still finds dispatchable work in the worklog; the cooldown is reserved for a genuinely empty backlog.
- [ ] AC2: The 30-min check-in must not be suppressed by the no-candidate cooldown (or the cooldown must not exceed the check-in cadence), so a re-offer can land during the pause and dispatch resumes promptly.
- [ ] AC3: Headless/unit coverage proving that with N free slots, ≥2 dispatchable candidates, and a single-entry coordination file, the worker dispatches at least once per minimum(noCandidateCooldownMs, 2× checkInIntervalMs) rather than per noCandidateCooldownMs.
data.title: Downtime dispatch stalls ~60 of every 62 minutes despite free slots (empty coordination file → 1h no-candidate cooldown)

# Leader lease expires during the no-candidate cooldown and can never refresh — zombie leader with divergent double-dispatch risk

## Problem statement

A downtime leader's 5-minute lease (`downtime-leader-lease.json`, TTL 300 s, `packages/herdr/src/leader-election.ts`) silently dies during the **1-hour no-candidate cooldown** (see WL-0MTEZ4XZJ006Y9U7) and can never be renewed. The worker keeps dispatching anyway via its cached `leaderState`, becoming a zombie leader with an expired lease. Any second herdr instance pointing at the same worklog can then win a fresh election and dispatch **concurrently** with the zombie → double dispatch of the same coordination entries.

Observed: the Tableau-Card-Engine lease has been frozen since `2026-08-27T18:01:09Z` (leaderId `22a6e7c7…`) while that same instance checked in and dispatched normally on Aug 29 (19:28, 20:30, 21:32, 22:35Z). The ContextHub lease (`2a3f2a88…`, acquired 22:47:26Z) will hit the same state ~5 min after its first cooldown begins.

## Root cause chain (code-verified)

1. `tick()` short-circuits during cooldown BEFORE the leader block, so `refreshLease()` is never called for the full `noCandidateCooldownMs` (60 min) >> lease TTL (5 min).
2. On cooldown expiry the leader block runs `if (leaderState) leaderManager.refreshLease()`.
3. `refreshLease()` guards with `if (!this.isLeader()) return`, and `isLeader()` requires `isLeaseValid(lease)` — an *unexpired* lease with `> MIN_VALID_LEASE_TTL_MS` remaining.
4. Because the lease expired during cooldown, `isLeader()` returns false → `refreshLease()` silently no-ops → **the lease can never be renewed by this instance again**.
5. The non-leader election branch is unreachable (cached `leaderState` stays true), so no re-election happens internally; the zombie continues to poll, check in, and dispatch with an expired lease.
6. A competing instance sees the stale/expired lease (`detectStaleLeader` → `cleanupStaleElection` → `attemptElection`) and becomes leader **while the zombie keeps dispatching** → both instances dispatch from the same coordination file → duplicate panes / duplicate claims (CAS claim mitigates double-claim of the same item, but different items can be claimed by both simultaneously, exceeding slot budgets).

## Evidence

- `downtime-leader-lease.json` (TCE): mtime + content frozen Aug 27 19:01 local while `downtime-dispatches.log` shows dispatches >48 h later.
- Code trace: cooldown short-circuit precedes the leader block (line ~2500 region of `downtime-worker.ts`); `refreshLease`/`isLeader` contract in `leader-election.ts` (`isLeaseValid` requires `remaining > MIN_VALID_LEASE_TTL_MS`).
- ContextHub: fresh lease acquired 22:47:26Z; same failure mode will recur at its first cooldown.

## Required fix (ACs)

- [ ] AC1: The leader must refresh (or at least consider renewing) its lease during the no-candidate cooldown, or the cooldown must refresh the lease on exit, so an alive leader never holds an expired lease.
- [ ] AC2: `refreshLease()` must renew an owned-but-expired lease (self-heal) instead of no-oping, and/or `leaderState` must be re-derived (not cached) each tick so an expired lease triggers a re-election instead of zombie dispatch.
- [ ] AC3: While non-leader with a valid lease held by another live instance, the worker must stay silent (current behavior — preserved). Add a test proving that two instances pointing at one coordination dir can never both dispatch simultaneously, including the zombie case.
data.title: Leader lease expires during no-candidate cooldown and can never refresh — zombie leader double-dispatch risk
